graph.name: Plan an ensemble scene
graph.description:
Suggest one or two active voices based on the supplied cast and scene.

Lesson: Use a shared public Context to choose a focal pair, while distinguishing speaking roles from ambient presence. A speaker-count request is advisory, not a hidden validator.

Limitations: A requested speaking limit is guidance, not a validator. Separate secret context for every speaker is not part of this recipe.

Opening installs an unassigned copy. Bind local model roles and provide the documented evidence before running.

Pre: at most 1 auxiliary calls. Preview before publishing or applying.

Try changing:
Change the focal pair from Mira/Sol to the two characters named by a new supplied dispute; check that everyone else's established actions remain intact.
Change the requested speaking count from two to one; compare whether the plan keeps the unanswered side of the dispute available for the next turn.

Documentation specimen (does not seed chat or actor memory):

Situation: Five companions are at the table; the question concerns Mira's debt to Sol.

Direction: Focus on Mira and Sol. Keep others present through supplied actions rather than giving everyone a response.

Sources and preparation: Inspect Five at the table, then Focus. This is shared supplied public context. It neither infers who witnessed an event nor creates separate secret context for each speaker.

Interpretation and output: Inspect the plan, then Guidance. Analysis is configured locally. A later Context Lens subgraph could expose Context→Context for Focus; keep the host source and Guidance terminal in the parent.

Five at the table (pre-scene)
Purpose: Read eight exchanges and selected character material so the debt question and the cast's established presence are available together.
Fixture: Chat: Mira, Sol, Rin, Kesh and Oren sit at the table. Rin sorts papers; Kesh holds the lamp; Oren watches the door. Rowan asks Mira whether she will repay Sol's debt. The player controls Rowan. No repayment decision is settled.
Inspect: Verify all supplied names, ambient actions and the ownership boundary. The active character source is not an automatic private card lookup for every cast member.

Debt and cast presence (pre-focus)
Purpose: Select supplied Context deterministically using the recent-message protection, literal pins and token target; remove oldest nonmandatory messages first.
Inspect: Check whether the focal conflict and ambient actions survived selection. No compression request is made; increase the budget if protected scene material cannot fit. Purpose and the completion cap do not affect Select. Retention follows keepRecent, literal pins and oldest-message removal; semantic relevance belongs in a model-backed step.

Mira and Sol take the beat (pre-plan)
Purpose: Produce a focal-cast Guidance plan rather than requiring each present character to deliver a line.
Inspect: Expect one focal exchange and selective ambient presence. Check cast continuity and whether the plan invents an opinion just to include an idle character.

Output tokens includes visible text and any reasoning tokens counted by the provider. A truncated result is discarded; inspect the error, then manually raise the cap and rerun. No automatic retry occurs. The 4096-token completion cap includes provider reasoning; the final plan targets 180 words, and Guidance independently enforces its 400-token budget.

Ensemble spotlight brief (pre-guidance)
Purpose: Deliver a compact focal-cast brief without spending the output budget on a separate instruction for every character.
Inspect: Inspect the Host result's proposed speakers and supplied ambient actions. The final writer may exceed the requested speaking count; review its actual reply.

pre-focus.title: Context Focus
pre-focus.purpose: Keep Mira's debt to Sol, Rowan's question, all five present cast members and their supplied actions. Drop unrelated individual backstory before dropping present scene evidence.

pre-plan.title: Response Plan
pre-plan.alias: Mira and Sol take the beat
pre-plan.instructions: Plan the debt-table response with at most two speaking NPCs: Mira and Sol, if both have a reason to speak. Label Focal exchange, Ambient presence, Player boundary. Give the debt question the spotlight; do not force a round-robin response. Keep Rin sorting papers, Kesh holding the lamp and Oren watching the door only where those supplied actions help orientation. Do not invent opinions or secret knowledge for them. Leave Rowan's dialogue, feelings and next choice to the player. Do not settle repayment unless present evidence already does. Keep the final plan within 180 words.
